claim: The mammalian heartbeat is thought to begin just prior to the linear heart tube stage of development.
source: The mammalian heartbeat is thought to begin just prior to the linear heart tube stage of development.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that references established scientific understanding about when the heartbeat begins.

claim: Randomly distributed spontaneous asynchronous Ca2+-oscillations (SACOs) were observed in the forming cardiac crescent (stage E7.75) prior to overt beating.
source: Using high-resolution live imaging of mouse embryos, we observed randomly distributed spontaneous asynchronous Ca2+-oscillations (SACOs) in the forming cardiac crescent (stage E7.75) prior to overt beating.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations using high-resolution live imaging of mouse embryos as described in the abstract.

claim: Nascent contraction initiated at around E8.0.
source: Nascent contraction initiated at around E8.0 and was associated with sarcomeric assembly and rapid Ca2+ transients, underpinned by sequential expression of the Na+-Ca2+ exchanger (NCX1) and L-type Ca2+ channel (LTCC).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the study reported in the abstract.

claim: Nascent contraction was associated with sarcomeric assembly and rapid Ca2+ transients.
source: Nascent contraction initiated at around E8.0 and was associated with sarcomeric assembly and rapid Ca2+ transients, underpinned by sequential expression of the Na+-Ca2+ exchanger (NCX1) and L-type Ca2+ channel (LTCC).
evidence: This association is reported as an observation from the study in the abstract.

claim: Sequential expression of NCX1 and LTCC underpins nascent contraction.
source: Nascent contraction initiated at around E8.0 and was associated with sarcomeric assembly and rapid Ca2+ transients, underpinned by sequential expression of the Na+-Ca2+ exchanger (NCX1) and L-type Ca2+ channel (LTCC).
evidence: This is reported as a finding from the study in the abstract.

claim: NCX1 plays an essential early role in establishing SACOs through to the initiation of beating.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of NCX1 and LTCC revealed rapid development of Ca2+ handling in the early heart and an essential early role for NCX1 in establishing SACOs through to the initiation of beating.
evidence: This conclusion is based on pharmacological inhibition experiments described in the abstract.

claim: NCX1 blockade impacted on CaMKII signalling to down-regulate cardiac gene expression.
source: NCX1 blockade impacted on CaMKII signalling to down-regulate cardiac gene expression, leading to impaired differentiation and failed crescent maturation.
evidence: This is a finding from the study reported in the abstract.

claim: NCX1 blockade led to impaired differentiation and failed crescent maturation.
source: NCX1 blockade impacted on CaMKII signalling to down-regulate cardiac gene expression, leading to impaired differentiation and failed crescent maturation.
evidence: This is a consequence observed from NCX1 blockade experiments reported in the abstract.

claim: The heart is the first organ to form and function during mammalian embryonic development.
source: The heart is the first organ to form and function during mammalian embryonic development.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge in the introduction.

claim: In the mouse, mesoderm originating from the primitive streak forms a bilateral pool of progenitor cells that at E7.5 give rise to the cardiac crescent.
source: In the mouse, mesoderm originating from the primitive streak forms a bilateral pool of progenitor cells that at E7.5 give rise to the cardiac crescent (CC).
evidence: This is a statement of established developmental biology knowledge.

claim: Between E8.25 and E8.5, the two sides of the cardiac crescent fuse and form the linear heart tube.
source: The CC subsequently expands and migrates to the midline whereupon, between E8.25 and E8.5, the two sides of the CC fuse and form the linear heart tube (LHT) (reviewed in Buckingham et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: The first cardiac contractions have been described during the transition from cardiac crescent to linear heart tube.
source: The first cardiac contractions have been described during the transition from CC to LHT.
evidence: This is a statement about what has been previously described in the literature.

claim: Early descriptions of initial cardiac contractions lack resolution.
source: Early descriptions of initial cardiac contractions (Navaratnam et al., 1986), including suggested pacemaker activity on either side of the embryonic midline (Goss, 1952), as well as optical mapping of spontaneous action potentials performed in both chicken (7 somite stage) and rat (3-somite stage) (Fujii et al., 1981; Hirota et al., 1985), have been informative, but lack resolution.
evidence: This is a critical assessment of previous studies cited in the introduction.

claim: Subsequent studies in mouse (3-somite stage) could only infer early electrical activity based on irregular fluctuations in basal Ca2+.
source: Subsequent studies in mouse (3-somite stage) could only infer early electrical activity based on irregular fluctuations in basal Ca2+ (Nishii and Shibata, 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about previous research findings supported by a citation.

claim: Forces exerted by cardiac contractions have been shown to be required for proper heart development.
source: This is especially important as the forces exerted by cardiac contractions have been shown in several models to be required for proper heart development (Granados-Riveron and Brook, 2012), and to modulate gene expression (Miyasaka et al., 2011) at later developmental stages.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cardiac contractions modulate gene expression at later developmental stages.
source: This is especially important as the forces exerted by cardiac contractions have been shown in several models to be required for proper heart development (Granados-Riveron and Brook, 2012), and to modulate gene expression (Miyasaka et al., 2011) at later developmental stages.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In mature cardiomyocytes, coordinated electrical excitation is coupled to physical contraction in a process termed excitation contraction coupling (ECC).
source: In mature cardiomyocytes, coordinated electrical excitation is coupled to physical contraction in a process termed excitation contraction coupling (ECC) (Bers, 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge about mature cardiomyocytes supported by a citation.

claim: ECC relies on changes in the intracellular concentration of Ca2+ via release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum in a process termed Ca2+ induced Ca2+ release (CICR).
source: ECC relies on changes in the intracellular concentration of the second messenger Ca2+ via release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) in a process termed Ca2+ induced Ca2+ release (CICR) (Fabiato and Fabiato, 1979).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Increases in the concentration of intracellular Ca2+ result in cardiomyocyte contraction due to Ca2+ binding to troponin and myofilament activation.
source: Increases in the concentration of intracellular Ca2+ result in cardiomyocyte contraction due to Ca2+ binding to troponin and myofilament activation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of cardiomyocyte contraction.

claim: Targeted disruption of genes encoding ECC proteins in mice has shown that contractile activity of immature cardiomyocytes does not require ECC.
source: Targeted disruption of genes encoding ECC proteins in mice has shown that contractile activity of immature cardiomyocytes does not require ECC.
evidence: This is a statement about findings from genetic studies in mice.

claim: Embryonic cardiomyocytes have a less developed SR and T-tubule system as well as an increased requirement for sarcolemmal Ca2+ flux.
source: Embryonic cardiomyocytes have a less developed SR and T-tubule system as well as an increased requirement for sarcolemmal Ca2+ flux (Conway et al., 2002; Seki et al., 2003)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Embryonic cardiomyocytes express a variety of ion channels and exchangers present in the adult heart.
source: and whilst they express a variety of ion channels and exchangers present in the adult heart (Seisenberger et al., 2000; Cribbs et al., 2001; Linask et al., 2001), the expression and activity of these proteins is distinct from that in mature cardiomyocytes (Liang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The expression and activity of ion channels and exchangers in embryonic cardiomyocytes is distinct from that in mature cardiomyocytes.
source: and whilst they express a variety of ion channels and exchangers present in the adult heart (Seisenberger et al., 2000; Cribbs et al., 2001; Linask et al., 2001), the expression and activity of these proteins is distinct from that in mature cardiomyocytes (Liang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Early studies suggested that myocyte contraction is triggered by sarcolemmal Ca2+ influx through voltage activated Ca2+ channels with little or no contribution from the SR.
source: Early studies suggested that myocyte contraction is triggered by sarcolemmal Ca2+ influx through voltage activated Ca2+ channels with little or no contribution from the SR (Nakanishi et al., 1988; Takeshima et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a statement about previous research findings supported by citations.

claim: At ~E8.5–9, Ca2+ transients originate from the SR, via RyR together with InsP3 channels, to trigger electrical activity as well as contraction.
source: In contrast, more recently it has been shown that at ~E8.5–9, Ca2+ transients originate from the SR, via RyR together with InsP3 channels, to trigger electrical activity as well as contraction (Viatchenko-Karpinski et al., 1999; Méry et al., 2005; Sasse et al., 2007; Rapila et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to more recent studies.

claim: Previous studies characterizing SR function at ~E8.5–9 did not investigate how Ca2+ transients are regulated at the earliest stages of cardiac crescent development when contraction is initiated.
source: Whilst these studies characterised SR function at ~E8.5–9, they did not investigate how Ca2+ transients are regulated at the earliest stages of cardiac crescent development when contraction is initiated, and relied on experiments performed using isolated cells cultured for between 12 to 70 hr (Sasse et al., 2007; Rapila et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a critical assessment of previous studies with citations.

claim: Four stages (0, 1, 2 and 3) of cardiac crescent development prior to the LHT stage were defined based on clear morphological differences.
source: On this basis, we defined four stages (0, 1, 2 and 3) of cardiac crescent development prior to the LHT stage, based on clear morphological differences.
evidence: This is a methodological approach described in the Results section.

claim: Stage 0 hearts represented the first discernible crescent structure situated beneath the developing head folds, being the widest (360–390 µm along the medio-lateral axis) and thinnest (70–80 µm along the rostro-caudal axis) of the crescent stages.
source: Stage 0 hearts represented the first discernible crescent structure situated beneath the developing head folds, being the widest (360–390 µm along the medio-lateral axis) and thinnest (70–80 µm along the rostro-caudal axis) of the crescent stages (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is a morphological characterization based on measurements from the study.

claim: At stage 1, the cardiac crescent had become narrower (300–370 µm) and thicker (75–95 µm).
source: Whilst stage 1 was morphologically similar to stage 0, the cardiac crescent had become narrower (300–370 µm) and thicker (75–95 µm).
evidence: This is a morphological characterization based on measurements from the study.

claim: By stage 2, folding of the cardiac crescent is evident based on the formation of a trough at the embryonic midline and two lobes on either side.
source: By stage 2, folding of the cardiac crescent is evident based on the formation of a trough at the embryonic midline and two lobes on either side.
evidence: This is a morphological observation from the study.

claim: At stage 0, cTnT was the most evident contractile protein within the early cardiac crescent, albeit without sarcomeric banding.
source: At stage 0, cTnT was the most evident contractile protein within the early cardiac crescent, albeit without sarcomeric banding (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from immunostaining experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Both α-Actinin and Myomesin appeared in small clusters of cells at stage 0.
source: Both α-Actinin and Myomesin appeared in small clusters of cells at stage 0 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from immunostaining shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Sarcomeric banding of α-Actinin and Myomesin, indicative of contractile capability, only manifested later in discrete regions within stage 1 and 2 crescents.
source: Sarcomeric banding of these proteins, indicative of contractile capability, only manifested later in discrete regions within stage 1 and 2 crescents (Figure 1B,C; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is an observation from immunostaining shown in Figures 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: By stage 3, sarcomere assembly and myofibrilar banding became more uniform, coincident with coalescence of the paired crescent primordia to the embryonic midline.
source: By stage 3, sarcomere assembly and myofibrilar banding became more uniform, coincident with coalescence of the paired crescent primordia to the embryonic midline.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: Myom1, Actn2 and Tnnt2 expression significantly increased between stages 0 and 1.
source: Myom1, Actn2 and Tnnt2 expression significantly increased between stages 0 and 1 and continued to increase until formation of the LHT (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1F and Supplementary file 1b.

claim: The onset of beating was observed in discrete foci in the lateral regions of cardiac crescents at stage 1.
source: Coincident with sarcomere formation at stage 1 (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), we observed the onset of beating in discrete foci in the lateral regions of cardiac crescents of cultured mouse embryos, by differential interference contrast (DIC) imaging (Video 1), significantly earlier than previously described (Navaratnam et al., 1986; Nishii and Shibata, 2006).
evidence: This is an observation from DIC imaging shown in Video 1.

claim: Beating foci generally contracted at the same rate, indicative of either synchronization or a shared intrinsic beat rate for nascent cardiomyocytes.
source: These foci generally contracted at the same rate, indicative of either synchronization or a shared intrinsic beat rate for nascent cardiomyocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the study shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The earliest cardiac contractions had a frequency of approximately 30 beats per minute (BPM).
source: The earliest cardiac contractions had a frequency of approximately 30 beats per minute (BPM), which increased significantly by stage 3 (after approximately 5 hr) to around 60 BPM (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Beat rate increased significantly by stage 3 to around 60 BPM.
source: The earliest cardiac contractions had a frequency of approximately 30 beats per minute (BPM), which increased significantly by stage 3 (after approximately 5 hr) to around 60 BPM (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study shown in Figure 2A.

claim: From stage 1 crescents until late stage 3, lateral propagation of Ca2+ transients was observed across the embryonic midline.
source: From stage 1 crescents until late stage 3, lateral propagation of Ca2+ transients was observed across the embryonic midline (Figure 2B), even through regions of non-contractile tissue (Video 2).
evidence: This is an observation from Ca2+ imaging shown in Figure 2B and Video 2.

claim: At stage 0 spontaneous asynchronous Ca2+ oscillations (SACOs) were observed within the forming crescent, in the absence of contractile activity and sarcomeric banding of cTnT.
source: At stage 0 spontaneous asynchronous Ca2+ oscillations (SACOs) were observed within the forming crescent, in the absence of contractile activity and sarcomeric banding of cTnT (Figure 2C; Video 3).
evidence: This is an observation from Ca2+ imaging shown in Figure 2C and Video 3.

claim: SACOs were observed in all stage 0 cardiac crescents imaged (n = 35).
source: SACOs were observed in all stage 0 cardiac crescents imaged (n = 35), propagated within individual cells (Figure 2D'') and displayed a range of Ca2+ dynamics with variable frequencies and durations (Figure 2D', Video 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the study with n=35 embryos.

claim: SACOs propagated within individual cells.
source: SACOs were observed in all stage 0 cardiac crescents imaged (n = 35), propagated within individual cells (Figure 2D'') and displayed a range of Ca2+ dynamics with variable frequencies and durations (Figure 2D', Video 4).
evidence: This is an observation from Ca2+ imaging shown in Figure 2D''.

claim: SACOs displayed a range of Ca2+ dynamics with variable frequencies and durations.
source: SACOs were observed in all stage 0 cardiac crescents imaged (n = 35), propagated within individual cells (Figure 2D'') and displayed a range of Ca2+ dynamics with variable frequencies and durations (Figure 2D', Video 4).
evidence: This is an observation from Ca2+ imaging shown in Figure 2D' and Video 4.

claim: SACOs were significantly slower than Ca2+ transients at later stages, with fluorescence reaching peak intensity between 0.79 and 11.9 s.
source: Compared to Ca2+ transients at later stages (Figure 2A) SACOs were significantly slower, with fluorescence reaching peak intensity between 0.79 and 11.9 s and decreasing with a similar slow rate of efflux (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: During a ~20 s recording period, only 10.3 ± 0.7 individual SACOs per embryo (n = 35) were observed occurring in different sites.
source: During a ~20 s recording period we observed only 10.3 ± 0.7 individual SACOs per embryo (n = 35) occurring in different sites.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the study with n=35 embryos.

claim: SACOs in individual cells occur at a frequency < 3 bpm.
source: Consecutive SACOs in the same site were rarely observed within the 20 s imaging window and, therefore, we conclude that SACOs in individual cells occur at a frequency < 3 bpm.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that consecutive SACOs in the same site were rarely observed within 20 s.

claim: Between E7.75 and stage 0, Slc8a1 significantly increased 21 fold (p-value<0.001).
source: Between E7.75 (as defined by the presence of clear head-folds but not a cardiac crescent) and stage 0, Slc8a1 significantly increased 21 fold (p-value<0.001), whilst Cacna1c revealed a modest but non-significant increase of 2.5 fold (p-value>0.05) and Cacna1d a significant 4-fold increase (p-value <0.01).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from qRT-PCR data.

claim: Between E7.75 and stage 0, Cacna1c revealed a modest but non-significant increase of 2.5 fold (p-value>0.05).
source: Between E7.75 (as defined by the presence of clear head-folds but not a cardiac crescent) and stage 0, Slc8a1 significantly increased 21 fold (p-value<0.001), whilst Cacna1c revealed a modest but non-significant increase of 2.5 fold (p-value>0.05) and Cacna1d a significant 4-fold increase (p-value <0.01).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from qRT-PCR data.

claim: Between E7.75 and stage 0, Cacna1d significantly increased 4-fold (p-value <0.01).
source: Between E7.75 (as defined by the presence of clear head-folds but not a cardiac crescent) and stage 0, Slc8a1 significantly increased 21 fold (p-value<0.001), whilst Cacna1c revealed a modest but non-significant increase of 2.5 fold (p-value>0.05) and Cacna1d a significant 4-fold increase (p-value <0.01).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from qRT-PCR data.

claim: From stage 1 onwards Slc8a1, Cacna1c and Cacna1d expression continued to significantly increase until stage 3.
source: From stage 1 onwards Slc8a1, Cacna1c and Cacna1d expression continued to significantly increase until stage 3 (Figure 3A,B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Slc8a1, 234-fold; Cacna1c, 38-fold; Cacna1d, 41-fold).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3A,B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: NCX1 was clearly detectable within the cardiac crescent at stage 0.
source: Whilst NCX1 was clearly detectable within the cardiac crescent at stage 0 (Figure 3D), CaV1.2 was absent (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an observation from immunostaining shown in Figure 3D.

claim: CaV1.2 was absent from the cardiac crescent at stage 0.
source: Whilst NCX1 was clearly detectable within the cardiac crescent at stage 0 (Figure 3D), CaV1.2 was absent (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an observation from immunostaining shown in Figure 3E.

claim: At stage 2 onwards, after established contraction, both NCX1 and CaV1.2 were expressed.
source: Differences in the expression of NCX1 and LTCC prior to beating were not maintained at later stages, after established contraction (stage 2 onwards), when both channels were expressed (Figure 3H,I).
evidence: This is an observation from immunostaining shown in Figure 3H,I.

claim: Acute treatment with NCX inhibitors (CB-DMB and KB-R7943) or LTCC inhibitor (Nifedipine) affected the embryos in a stage dependent-manner.
source: Acute treatment (for a maximum of 30 min) with NCX inhibitors (CB-DMB and KB-R7943) or LTCC inhibitor (Nifedipine), affected the embryos in a stage dependent-manner (Figure 4).
evidence: This is an observation from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Both NCX1 and the LTCC were required for Ca2+ transients during stages 1 and 2.
source: Both NCX1 and the LTCC were required for Ca2+ transients during stages 1 and 2 (Figure 4A), and their inhibition led to an initial confinement of Ca2+ transients to one side of the crescent (within approximately 5 min of treatment, which persisted through to 15 min) followed shortly afterwards by complete loss of Ca2+ signal (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological inhibition experiments shown in Figure 4A,C,D.

claim: At stage 3 and later, only the LTCC was required for Ca2+ transient generation.
source: At stage 3 and later, only the LTCC was required for Ca2+ transient generation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological inhibition experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Treatment of stage 0 embryos with CB-DMB resulted in a 90% decrease in the number of cells with SACOs after drug application when compared to baseline.
source: Treatment of stage 0 embryos with CB-DMB and KB-R7943 resulted in a 90% decrease in the number of cells with SACOs after drug application when compared to baseline. This was significantly greater than following application of nifedipine to inhibit LTCC, or the DMSO control (CB-DMB, 90% inhibition + 6.6, mean + SEM, n = 10 embryos, p-value <0.01; KB-R7943, 91% inhibition + 7.0, n = 9 embryos, p-value <0.001; nifedipine, 39% inhibition + 11.4; n = 8 embryos, p-value=0.44; DMSO, 29% inhibition + 7.6, n = 10; Figure 4H–J; Supplementary file 1d).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 4H-J.

claim: Treatment of stage 0 embryos with KB-R7943 resulted in a 91% decrease in the number of cells with SACOs after drug application when compared to baseline.
source: Treatment of stage 0 embryos with CB-DMB and KB-R7943 resulted in a 90% decrease in the number of cells with SACOs after drug application when compared to baseline. This was significantly greater than following application of nifedipine to inhibit LTCC, or the DMSO control (CB-DMB, 90% inhibition + 6.6, mean + SEM, n = 10 embryos, p-value <0.01; KB-R7943, 91% inhibition + 7.0, n = 9 embryos, p-value <0.001; nifedipine, 39% inhibition + 11.4; n = 8 embryos, p-value=0.44; DMSO, 29% inhibition + 7.6, n = 10; Figure 4H–J; Supplementary file 1d).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from pharmacological experiments shown in Figure 4H-J.

claim: NCX1 is required for establishing the earliest pre-contractile SACOs.
source: These data suggest that NCX1 is required for establishing the earliest pre-contractile SACOs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the pharmacological inhibition experiments.

claim: Chronic treatment of Eomes-GFP ESC cultures with CB-DMB or Nifedipine resulted in a reduction in the percentage of beating EBs at day 14.
source: Chronic treatment of Eomes-GFP ESC cultures (ESCs containing a knock-in of a GFP reporter into the endogenous Eomes locus (Arnold et al., 2009); marking nascent mesoderm (Ciruna and Rossant, 1999), with CB-DMB or Nifedipine, from days 0 to 14 of differentiation, resulted in a reduction in the percentage of beating EBs at day 14, down to 22% and 52% (Percentage beating EBs; DMSO, 76.53% (n = 196); CB-DMB, 22.37%, p-value<0.001 (n = 152); Nifedipine, 52.11%, p-value<0.001 [n = 71]) in the presence of CB-DMB and nifedipine respectively, compared to controls (Figure 5A)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from chronic drug treatment experiments shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The reduction in beating EBs was supported by a down-regulation of key cardiac genes Myh6 and Tnnt2 specifically following treatment with CB-DMB relative to control DMSO treatment.
source: The reduction in beating EBs was supported by a down-regulation of key cardiac genes Myh6 (mean+ SEM: 0.57 ± 0.058; p-value<0.05; n = 6; Figure 5B) and Tnnt2 (0.66 ± 0.095; p-value<0.05; n = 6; Figure 5B) specifically following treatment with CB-DMB relative to control DMSO treatment.
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Culture in 0.1 mM Ca2+ resulted in an inhibitory effect on EB beating to the same extent as with CB-DMB treatment.
source: Culture in 0.1 mM Ca2+ resulted in an inhibitory effect on EB beating to the same extent (percentage beating EBs; 1.8 mM, 78.38%, n = 74; 0.1 mM, 28.75%, n = 80; p-value<0.001) as with CB-DMB treatment (Figure 5C)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experiments with reduced Ca2+ shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Following CB-DMB-induced NCX1 inhibition at day 7 of EB differentiation, activated phospho-CaMKII (pCaMKII) levels were significantly reduced compared to either DMSO control or nifedipine treatment.
source: Following CB-DMB-induced NCX1 inhibition at day 7 of EB differentiation, activated phospho-CaMKII (pCaMKII) levels were significantly reduced compared to either DMSO control or nifedipine treatment (mean ± SEM: DMSO, 1.18 ± 0.13; CB-DMB, 0.69 ± 0.15; nifedipine, 1.13 ± 0.06. DMSO vs. CB-DMB, p-value<0.01; CB-DMB vs. nifedipine, p-value<0.05; n = 3; Figure 5D,D').
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from Western blot analysis shown in Figure 5D,D'.

claim: NCX1 inhibition reduced Ca2+ influx and decreased activation of CaMKII accompanied by significantly reduced expression of Mef2c and Myh7 relative to DMSO control.
source: NCX1 inhibition reduced Ca2+ influx and decreased activation of CaMKII accompanied by significantly reduced expression of Mef2c and Myh7 relative to DMSO control (mean ± SEM: Mef2c, 0.71 ± 0.13; Myh7, 0.55 ± 0.18; p-value<0.05; n = 6) which, whilst previously associated with pathological cardiac hypertrophy, contribute here towards (physiological) cardiomyocyte differentiation (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Embryos cultured in the presence of CB-DMB had reduced expression of cTnT compared to embryos cultured in other conditions.
source: More specifically embryos cultured in the presence of CB-DMB had reduced expression of cTnT compared to embryos cultured in other conditions.
evidence: This is an observation from embryo culture experiments shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Most cells in CB-DMB treated embryos were still positive for Nkx2.5, suggesting delayed or impaired differentiation likely accounted for the failure of crescent formation under conditions of NCX1 blockade.
source: However, most cells were still positive for Nkx2.5, suggesting delayed or impaired differentiation likely accounted for the failure of crescent formation under conditions of NCX1 blockade.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on immunostaining observations.

claim: While Tnnt2 was down-regulated in both CB-DMB and Nifedipine treated embryos, Nkx2.5 was only down-regulated in CB-DMB treated embryos.
source: While Tnnt2 was down-regulated in both CB-DMB and Nifedipine treated embryos, Nkx2.5 was only down-regulated in CB-DMB treated embryos (Figure 5F,G).
evidence: This is supported by qRT-PCR data from cultured embryos shown in Figure 5F,G.

claim: Spontaneous asynchronous calcium oscillations (SACOs) within the forming cardiac crescent have not previously been reported in any type of excitable cell.
source: The observation of spontaneous asynchronous calcium oscillations (SACOs) within the forming cardiac crescent was a surprising finding that, to the best of our knowledge, has not previously been reported in any type of excitable cell.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding in the Discussion.

claim: SACOs are required in cells that need to optimally activate Ca2+-dependent signalling (via the CAMKII pathway) in order to up-regulate genes necessary for further differentiation and morphogenesis.
source: The specific role of SACOs is currently unknown and we hypothesise that they are required in cells that need to optimally activate Ca2+-dependent signalling (via the CAMKII pathway) in order to up-regulate genes necessary for further differentiation and morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors in the Discussion.

claim: In zebrafish embryos it has recently been demonstrated that Ca2+ handling and not contraction per se is essential for regulating cardiomyocyte development.
source: In zebrafish embryos it has recently been demonstrated that Ca2+ handling and not contraction per se is essential for regulating cardiomyocyte development (Andersen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Previous studies characterised functional expression of NCX from E8.5-E9.5 (post-LHT formation) in mouse coincident with cardiac looping and significantly later than the onset of the first heat beat described herein.
source: Previous studies characterised functional expression of NCX from E8.5-E9.5 (post-LHT formation) in mouse (Linask et al., 2001; Reppel et al., 2007) coincident with cardiac looping and significantly later than the onset of the first heat beat described herein.
evidence: This is a comparison with previous studies supported by citations.

claim: NCX1 knock-out mice have been generated by multiple groups, with conflicting results in regards to the phenotype, extent of mutant heart development and the stage at which embryonic lethality occurs.
source: NCX1 knock-out mice have been generated by multiple groups, with conflicting results in regards to the phenotype, extent of mutant heart development and the stage at which embryonic lethality occurs (Wakimoto et al., 2000; Koushik et al., 2001; Reuter et al., 2002; Cho et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a statement about previous genetic studies supported by citations.

claim: Loss of NCX1 may be compensated for at the level of early cardiomyocyte specification, differentiation and contraction.
source: This suggests that loss of NCX1 may be compensated for at the level of early cardiomyocyte specification, differentiation and contraction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the conflicting results from NCX1 knockout studies.

claim: In mammals there are three different Na+-Ca2+ exchangers (NCX1, NCX2 and NCX3), and these three exchangers share similar physiological properties.
source: In mammals there are three different Na+-Ca2+ exchangers (NCX1, NCX2 and NCX3), and it has been previously demonstrated that these three exchangers share similar physiological properties (Linck et al., 1998; Lytton, 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: NCX1 has several splicing variants with exon 1 being mutually exclusive to exon 2.
source: Furthermore, NCX1 has several splicing variants with exon 1 being mutually exclusive to exon 2 (Lytton, 2007; Quednau et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In all of the previous NCX1 generic loss-of-function studies, mutant mice were created by targeting exon 2, supporting the possibility that an alternately spliced variant may be able to compensate.
source: Indeed, in all of the previous NCX1 generic loss-of-function studies, mutant mice were created by targeting exon 2, supporting the possibility that an alternately spliced variant may be able to compensate.
evidence: This is an inference based on the design of previous genetic studies.

claim: Pharmacological channel blockers CB-DMB and KB-R7943 resulted in an acute stage-specific-loss of NCX1 function which attributed an essential role for NCX1 in generating SACOs.
source: In contrast, our use of pharmacological channel blockers CB-DMB and KB-R7943, resulted in an acute stage-specific-loss of NCX1 function which attributed an essential role for NCX1 in generating SACOs, and potentially acting as a trigger to establish the onset of beating in the cardiac crescent and subsequent cardiomyocyte differentiation and morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the pharmacological experiments in the study.

claim: These findings are consistent with the situation in tremblor (tre) zebrafish which have a mutation in NCX1 leading to absence of normal calcium transients and cardiac fibrillation.
source: These findings are consistent with the situation in tremblor (tre) zebrafish which have a mutation in NCX1 leading to absence of normal calcium transients and cardiac fibrillation (Langenbacher et al., 2005)

claim: Lowering the concentration of Ca2+ in the media had a similar effect on reducing the number of beating EBs as treatment with CB-DMB.
source: Parallel analyses on ESC-derived cardiomyocytes revealed that lowering the concentration of Ca2+ in the media had a similar effect on reducing the number of beating EBs as treatment with CB-DMB.
evidence: This is a finding from experiments with reduced extracellular Ca2+ shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The use of the inhibitor KB-R7943, previously reported to specifically inhibit reverse mode NCX1 activity, replicated observations made with CB-DMB.
source: Furthermore, our use of the inhibitor KB-R7943, previously reported to specifically inhibit reverse mode NCX1 activity (Brustovetsky et al., 2011), replicated observations made with CB-DMB, such that at stage 1 and 2 both LTCC and NCX1 are required for sufficient Ca2+ influx.
evidence: This is a finding from pharmacological experiments with KB-R7943 supported by a citation.

claim: Increased expression of NCX1 has been linked with pathological hypertrophy and heart failure.
source: Increased expression of NCX1 has also been linked with pathological hypertrophy and heart failure (reviewed in Sipido et al., 2002), whereby elevated NCX1 is thought to compensate for defective ECC and depressed function of SERCA but also produce arrhythmogenic-delayed after-depolarisations (Gómez et al., 1997; Schultz et al., 2004; Venetucci et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Transgenic mice over-expressing NCX1 within the myocardium exhibited a proportional decrease in contractile function and increased incidence of heart failure.
source: Transgenic mice over-expressing NCX1 within the myocardium exhibited a proportional decrease in contractile function and increased incidence of heart failure, suggesting a decompensatory mechanism with regards to Ca2+ handling (Roos et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Delta isoforms of CaMKII predominate in the heart and are involved in multiple signalling cascades to regulate gene expression, as well as cardiomyocyte physiology including Ca2+ and Na+ homeostasis.
source: Delta isoforms of CaMKII predominate in the heart and are involved in multiple signalling cascades to regulate gene expression, as well as cardiomyocyte physiology including Ca2+ and Na+ homeostasis (Wagner et al., 2006; Aiba et al., 2010).

claim: There is recent precedent for a role for Ca2+ in the establishment of other embryonic lineages; most notably Ca2+ signals are involved in the earliest steps of neurogenesis, including neural induction and the differentiation of neural progenitors into neurons.

claim: An early induction of Ca2+-handling preceding beating within cardiac muscle is pivotal for subsequent terminal differentiation and normal heart development.
